A1.justification: Both PDFs describe CodeTaste and provide readable main text, equations, figures, tables, and Appendices A–D. Corresponding material can be matched across revisions, renumbering, and relocation.

before.justification: v1 reports original evaluations of four coding agents on CodeTaste, including alignment, instruction following, functional correctness, precision, costs, and case studies.

after.justification: v2 reports original evaluations of five coding agents and adds a human rule audit, oracle-judge validation, language-level analysis, and significance tests.

M1.justification: Section 3.4 adds a post-generation filter that removes additive rules enforcing arbitrary implementation choices; Appendix A.3 identifies Gemini 3.1 Pro as the classifier. This extends the existing benchmark-construction method, while the refactoring agents' Direct, Plan, and Oracle Multiplan procedures remain unchanged.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate 100 refactoring instances from 87 repositories across the same six programming-language categories and the same tracks. The language breakdown analyzes retained coverage. v2 explicitly distinguishes its additional 150 released commits from the instances evaluated in the paper.

E2.justification: v2 adds MiniMax M2.7 to the four retained agents: GPT-5.2, GPT-5.1 Codex Mini, Sonnet 4.5, and Qwen3. Its results appear in the Instructed Track and all three Open Track modes, establishing an actual comparator addition.

E3.justification: The rule filter changes the scoring criteria throughout evaluation, reducing mean additive rules from 29.66 to 17.94. Section 4.1 revises the reported precision calculation and specifies filtered line sets for precision and patch size. New protocols include a 30-rule human audit and randomized six-plan judge control. These are substantive evaluation revisions; they do not establish that retained agent executions were rerun.

E4.justification: Beyond the retained mode comparisons and case studies, v2 adds an expert audit of restrictive rules, a control investigating oracle-selection bias, and performance breakdowns by language (Appendices A.3, A.6, and A.7). These substantially extend analysis of measurement validity and possible explanations for the results.

E5.justification: v1 already reports 95% confidence intervals and five test-suite calibration runs. v2 adds paired sign-flip permutation tests with 100,000 permutations and Benjamini–Hochberg correction, language-level standard errors, and Cohen's kappa for the human audit. This substantially expands statistical assessment without establishing additional repeated agent runs.

E6.justification: v2 broadly updates alignment, precision, and edit-size results and adds MiniMax and validation results. GPT-5.2 Open Track alignment changes from 7.7/14.1/19.4% to 7.9/15.1/20.6% across Direct/Plan/Multiplan; its instructed precision changes from 56.2% to 48.4% (v1 Tables 4–5; v2 Tables 5–6). These accompany revised scoring and should not be interpreted as same-setting performance gains. Some case-study scores also change.

T1.justification: Section 4.1 corrects reductive precision to intersect removed lines with rule coverage in the original repository R, rather than the patched repository. The symbolic-propagation example also corrects its witness enumeration. Most other definitions are retained or relocated, and no new theorem or proof is introduced.

C1.justification: The central contributions and instructed-versus-open performance gap remain. However, v2 corrects v1's introductory claim of single-digit alignment even with oracle support: below 8% is now explicitly restricted to Direct mode, while oracle-supported alignment reaches 20.6%. This materially qualifies the headline claim without redefining the contribution.

C2.justification: The new Limitations section explicitly addresses small-sample comparisons, uneven language coverage, valid refactorings outside the original human choice, and possible LLM-construction bias. Appendix A.6 also uses the new control to favor poorer candidate-plan quality over judge bias as an explanation for Sonnet's Multiplan decline. These substantially expand the boundaries and interpretation of the evaluation.

D1.justification: v2 identifies Gemini 3.1 Pro for rule filtering, documents MiniMax's configuration, and reports releasing 150 additional commits with descriptions and rule sets. Most environment specifications and prompts are retained. Conversely, Section 4.1 drops the explicit harness-version listing, including Qwen Code v0.6.2.

R1.justification: v2 adds a structured comparison of seven prior benchmarks in Table 1 and supporting citations concerning refactoring, static analysis, code benchmarks, and the new model. Most compared benchmarks were already discussed in v1, and the positioning around large, multilingual, human-intent refactoring remains. Bibliographic updates to existing works do not constitute new research coverage.

P1.justification: The main text undergoes extensive rewriting and explanatory restructuring: static-rule formalization moves into Section 2.1, construction steps receive clearer organization, and the introduction and conclusion are substantially revised. A dedicated Limitations section is added. The case-study and prompt appendices remain largely intact apart from corrections and updated references.

P2.justification: v2 redraws the pipeline and rule illustrations, reformats the instance-statistics display, relocates the metric diagram, and expands result displays. Figure 8 replaces the Open Track PASS panel with alignment, changes the IFR axis range, and adds MiniMax. New tables present benchmark comparisons, the human audit, language results, and significance summaries.

improvement.justification: v1 acknowledges arbitrary naming requirements as a scoring concern; v2 directly addresses them through filtering and an expert audit reporting 80% agreement (Appendix A.3). Together with the corrected precision definition, controlled judge analysis, significance testing, and explicit limitations, this substantially strengthens the central evaluation's validity and interpretability. The audit remains small and the oracle control has unexecuted alternatives, while some harness-version detail is lost, but these limitations do not outweigh the gains.
